A ray diagram showing refraction. A straight horizontal line represents the boundary between air (top, light blue) and water (bottom, darker blue). A vertical dashed line (the normal) passes through the boundary. A red incident ray comes from the top left, striking the boundary at the normal. The refracted ray continues into the water, bending closer to the normal. Angles 'i' (angle of incidence) and 'r' (angle of refraction) are marked between the rays and the normal.

A ray diagram showing lateral displacement. A rectangular glass block. An incident ray strikes the top at angle i. The ray refracts closer to the normal at angle r inside the block. It hits the bottom boundary and refracts away from the normal, emerging parallel to the original incident ray's path. A dashed straight line extends the original incident ray right through the block. A perpendicular line labeled 'd' (lateral displacement) connects the emergent ray to the dashed line.
